snapshot.description: Agile Mind publishes K–12 math and science programs licensed to school districts nationwide. They run Salesforce for pipeline management and QuickBooks Online for invoicing — but the two systems don't talk. Crystal re-keys every invoice. Holly tracks inventory in Excel. Maria can't see payment status without opening QB manually. The back-to-school peak (April–August) is a spreadsheet fire drill every year.
painPoints: Manual invoice entry from Salesforce agreements into QuickBooks — Crystal re-keys every deal
Live inventory not visible in Salesforce — Holly maintains a separate Excel demand worksheet
No automated payment sync — Maria runs manual QB reports to check invoice status
Print procurement decisions made on gut instinct, not data — overstock and shortage every season

talkingPoints.trigger: When they say 'we already have people handling this'
talkingPoints.say: That's exactly the problem — you're paying people to move data between systems instead of growing the business. Every hour Crystal spends re-keying invoices is an hour she's not doing higher-value finance work.
talkingPoints.impact: Reallocate Crystal's time from data entry to cash flow analysis

talkingPoints.trigger: When they push back on cost
talkingPoints.say: One missed or delayed invoice to a school district can push payment into next fiscal year. How many times per quarter does that happen? At an average contract value of even $50K, one recovery pays for months of our managed service.
talkingPoints.impact: One recovered invoice typically exceeds 3+ months of DataSkate fees

talkingPoints.trigger: When they ask about the timeline
talkingPoints.say: We scope to a 10-week delivery from signed SOW — before back-to-school season. Flow 1 (SF→QB invoice) typically goes live in week 6, so you'll have automated invoicing running before the April peak.
talkingPoints.impact: Live before the April–August procurement crunch

talkingPoints.trigger: When they mention the QuickBooks version uncertainty
talkingPoints.say: That's a one-question intake item we'll resolve before architecture. QBO means a native MuleSoft connector and faster delivery. Desktop is a different path — we've handled both. The intake form clarifies it in 24 hours.
talkingPoints.impact: Removes the biggest uncertainty before any commitment

openingLines.context: When opening with Maria (CFO / finance lead)
openingLines.line: Maria, how many hours per week does your team spend moving data from Salesforce into QuickBooks? Because for publishers at your revenue stage, that number is usually 8–12 hours — and it's the #1 thing we eliminate in week 6 of an engagement.

openingLines.context: When Crystal (the re-keyer) is in the room
openingLines.line: Crystal, imagine if every time a deal closed in Salesforce, the QuickBooks invoice was already there — correct line items, correct amounts — before you even opened QB. What would you do with those hours?

openingLines.context: When the conversation opens on back-to-school stress
openingLines.line: You just came out of the April crunch. Walk me through what Holly's spreadsheet looked like in week 3 — because what you describe is exactly what we built Flow 3 to replace.

aiJourneyNarrative: Phase 1 gets the plumbing in — Salesforce and QuickBooks talk, inventory is visible, Crystal stops re-keying. That alone reclaims 8–10 hours per week and eliminates a full category of billing errors. Phase 2 turns those live data connections into automated decisions: purchase recommendations trigger when pipeline demand exceeds stock, and invoice reminders go out without anyone scheduling them. Phase 3 is where it gets interesting — an AI agent reads opportunity stages, historical sell-through, and seasonal patterns to recommend exact print run quantities per title, weeks before the production deadline. You stop guessing how many Intensified Algebra SABs to order for next school year.
